history.summary: A Shiva temple inside the upper fort of Chitradurga, one of eighteen temples in the fort complex, and the most famous of them. It is linked to the Mahabharata legend of Bhima and the rakshasa Hidimba: the temple displays a giant tooth said to be Hidimba's, a large iron cylinder (about 3 m in circumference and 2 m high) known as the Bheri or Drum of Bhima, a monolithic pillar and two swing frames at its gate; tradition says Hidimba and his sister Hidimbi lived here, and that Bhima married Hidimbi (mother of Ghatotkacha) at this spot. A recent blog claims a 12th-century Hoysala inscription at the temple explicitly names it as the Bhima-Hidimbi marriage site and says the ASI has examined it (UNVERIFIED - based on a single non-authoritative source). The association of this region with the Pandavas is also reported at the Chandravalli caves about 3 km away. The fort's presiding Nayaka family deity was Ekanatheswari (Ekanathamma), whose temple also stands in the fort.

name: Hidimbeshwara Temple
town_description: Chitradurga, in central Karnataka about 200 km north-west of Bengaluru, is famed for its massive hill fort - the 'Stone Fort' (Yelu Suttina Kote, fort of seven walls) built between the 10th and 18th centuries by the Rashtrakutas, Chalukyas, Hoysalas, Vijayanagara and finally the Nayakas of Chitradurga, whose last ruler Madakari Nayaka fell to Hyder Ali in 1779. The fort houses eighteen temples and is associated with the heroism of Onake Obavva and the Bhima-Hidimba legend.
